items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: But they had so many bands and Buddy Bolden was just another trumpet player to me. But I've heard Buddy Bolden.

ctx.x: Could I ask you, Albert, you heard Buddy Bolden when you were a child. And I wonder if you could remember at all how he sounded and how the band played.

Well, I've had the pleasure to hear Buddy Bolden when I was a young lad, around seven, eight, six years old, something like that, the first time. He was playing at the Lincoln Park uptown. My Uncle Joe used to take me up there on Sundays. It was a matinee thing in the open air. And I've heard him two, three times. I wasn't impressed with him or nothing at the time because I wasn't interested in playing. But they had so many bands and Buddy Bolden was just another trumpet player to me. But I've heard Buddy Bolden.…

This is what I think, you know. Just my feeling about it is that there couldn't have just been one band that started the whole of the jazz ragtime thing off. There must have been lots of other musicians around that time.
